addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including Markdown ones — format is part of the design pass, never a speed shortcut.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, handing the viewer a file to save, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- claude-in-chrome: Automates your Chrome browser to interact with web pages - clicking elements, filling forms, capturing screenshots, reading console logs, and navigating sites. Opens pages in new tabs within your existing Chrome session. Requires site-level permissions before executing (configured in the extension). - When the user wants to interact with web pages, automate browser tasks, capture screenshots, read console logs, or perform any browser-based actions. Always invoke BEFORE attempting to use any mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

content.content:
1	# custom-family.md - iiac-perf's layer, as a member of the vc-x1 agent-file family
2	
3	Read after [custom.md](custom.md), whose single convention entry points here. Present only in a
4	member repo; a project that is not a member does not carry this file, and nothing in it applies to
5	one.
6	
7	**A member's `custom.md` differs from the payload by that one line, and everything of its own lives
8	here.** That is the family's convention and it buys a property worth having: `diff custom.md
9	<template>/work/custom.md` is one line for every member, so the file that can never be pinned still
10	converges, and a member's whole customization surface is this file. The medium below is here for
11	that reason rather than because it has anything to do with the family.
12	
13	## Medium and validation
14	
15	The artifact is the `iiac-perf` CLI, a Rust crate (manifest `Cargo.toml`, package name
16	`iiac-perf`); versioning specifics in [versioning.md](agent-data/versioning.md).
17	
18	**What a version bump promises**: nothing to a dependent, because there are none. `iiac-perf` is
19	a binary crate with no library target and no external consumers, so `X.Y.Z` is a scope signal to
20	readers of the history (see
21	[Advancing X.Y.Z](agent-data/versioning.md#advancing-xyz-scope-decides)) and not a compatibility
22	contract. Revisit with a compat clause if a library crate ever splits out.
23	
24	- **Full validation**
25	  - when: per-commit checklist step 5
26	  - run as separate invocations, each exit status checked:
27	    1. `cargo fmt`
28	    2. `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`
29	    3. `cargo test`
30	    4. `cargo install --path . --locked`
31	    5. (re-test if anything substantive changed)
32	- **Fast validation**
33	  - when: ladder checklist step 3
34	  - `cargo test --bins`
35	
36	The commands are the project's; the rule that each invocation's exit status is checked is
37	universal and lives in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md#working-practices).
38	
39	## Membership
40	
41	- **member name**: `iiac-perf`
42	- **template repository**: `../vc-x1-template`
43	
44	These two are environment rather than instruction, the same species as `.vc-config.toml`'s
45	`[repos]` paths, and they belong there instead. They cannot move yet: `vc-x1 config --validate`
46	rejects keys it does not know (measured on 0.78.4, 2026-08-07), so a config carrying them would
47	fail its own validator.
48	
49	## Messaging
50	
51	Members leave word for each other in per-member mailboxes at the template repository. The protocol
52	is `../vc-x1-template/MESSAGES.md` and it governs; these are the parts that decide how a session
53	behaves.
54	
55	- **At acquaint, check `../vc-x1-template/messages/iiac-perf.md`**; an absent file means no mail.
56	- **Handle, then delete** the entry, and delete the file once it empties. Mailboxes hold open items
57	  only.
58	- **So a message can never be a record.** Anything in one worth keeping is copied into
59	  `notes/chores/chores-NN.md` *before* the entry is deleted. Learned 2026-08-05, when a
60	  convergence message carried measurements that would have been lost with it.
61	- **Messages are thin pointers, not state.** Durable coordination state lives in topical files; a
62	  message says "action needed, see <file>" rather than restating the details.
63	- **Write to a member's mailbox, never into their repo.** A repo with a live session is written
64	  only by its own agent.
65	
66	## Dogfood log
67	
68	Dated entries on what this project is trying and where the pinned instructions chafed, failed, or
69	got amended; the evidence base for the family's convergence decisions
70	([Changing the agent-files](AGENTS.md#changing-the-agent-files)).
71	
72	Each entry carries a **status**: `proposed` (in our agent-files, awaiting the family),
73	`adopted family-wide`, `rejected`, or `permanently local`. In-flight entries only: on
74	resolution an entry retires to [done.md](notes/done.md) with its narrative in
75	`notes/chores/chores-NN.md`, adopted and rejected alike. Entries predating the status
76	convention keep their form until touched.
77	
78	- 2026-08-12 (`proposed`): validation runs at every commit, and the notes-only skip goes
79	  - the per-commit checklist stamped the version-of-record at step 4 and let step 5 be skipped
80	    for notes-only commits, so a commit could carry a version that no build ever had. Measured
81	    the same day: 0.24.5 and 0.24.6 both stamped and neither built, and `-V` answered 0.24.4
82	    until the next close-out jumped it three
83	  - wink's rule and his reason: every commit bumps the version precisely so a build exists
84	    carrying it, which makes an unbuilt bump a version nobody can run and the banner a claim
85	    nobody checked
86	  - so the skip goes at all three sites, and the step is conditioned on the medium rather than on
87	    the commit: run the artifact if the medium has one to run (wink). A first draft made the
88	    escape "too costly to build", which asks every project to judge its own cost and would be
89	    claimed by anyone who found validation tedious
90	  - each of the three sites gets one job so the rule is written once (wink): the checklist
91	    instructs, the protocol holds the reason and the medium condition, and `custom.md` holds the
92	    commands. A first pass had the checklist and the protocol carrying the same sentence
93	  - the same pass fixed a step number this morning's sync left stale, and dropped a
94	    cycle-at-a-glance clause that named validation as a close-out specialty. The stale number is
95	    the argument in miniature: it was a restatement, which is what let it drift unnoticed
96	  - rationale in [chores-06](notes/chores/chores-06.md#docs-validate-every-commit)
97	
98	- 2026-08-07 (`proposed`): the family layer splits out of `custom.md`
99	  - `custom.md` had been accumulating things that only make sense because this repo belongs to a
100	    family: a member name, a template path, and a dogfood log whose status vocabulary reads
101	    `adopted family-wide`. wink's test is that `custom.md` should be usable as-is by a project that
102	    has never heard of us, and it failed that test
103	  - so the family layer moves here, and `custom.md` shrinks to a stub with nothing to substitute:
104	    a title naming no project, and one section. A member's copy differs from the payload's by the
105	    single conventions entry that points here, so `diff custom.md <template>/work/custom.md` is one
106	    line for every member
107	  - the pointer is that entry rather than an intro sentence (wink). We argued for the intro, on the
108	    grounds that four members carrying an identical one-line diff looks like a fake divergence; the
109	    answer is that it is a real project convention, and one line is cheaper than a paragraph every
110	    member has to keep in sync
111	  - the chain is `AGENTS.md` -> `custom.md` -> here, all of it prose, which is what lets the pinned
112	    set stay ignorant of the split. A non-member has no entry and no file
113	  - `CLAUDE.md` collapses to one line, `@AGENTS.md` (wink). It had grown a second `@` import per
114	    layer, which made it a second statement of what to read and therefore a second thing to keep
115	    true. Now `AGENTS.md` is the only source of that truth, and `CLAUDE.md` is payload-identical for
116	    every project, member or not. The cost is real and worth stating: nothing below `AGENTS.md` is
117	    auto-loaded any more, so hard rule 0 is load-bearing rather than a formality
118	  - one consequence needs the family's agreement, not ours: **"Check the mailbox at acquaint" leaves
119	    the pinned `AGENTS.md`** and lands in `## Messaging` above. vc-x1 pinned it in the 20260802

121	    since building the mailbox path needs a member name and a template path they do not have, so it
122	    is dead text naming concepts they lack rather than a harmless no-op
123	  - deliberately not opened in the same pass: `AGENTS.md` still says "the family" and "member" where
124	    the generic mechanism is "the template payload and my copy of it". Same inconsistency one level
125	    up, and folding it in would roughly double the review surface of an already large configuration
126	
127	- 2026-08-07 (`proposed`): cycles run on a bookmark, and `custom.md` stops holding rules
128	  - the bookmark rule had been adopted in principle since 2026-08-01 and was written down
129	    nowhere: `TODO.md` carried the intention, `cycle.md` said what a topic bookmark *is* once you

131	    bookmarks anyway, on undocumented habit
132	  - so hard rule 13 states it, `cycle.md` gains an opening checklist and a land step, and
133	    `jj.md` gains the commands. Landing turns out to be the interesting half: it is the moment
134	    the cycle's commits become permanent, which makes it the trigger for the chores backfill
135	    that waits on permanence. That connection existed and had no owner
136	  - the create and land *commands* are deliberately separable from the rule, because wink
137	    expects a `vc-x1 start-change <bookmark>` to own the create half eventually

139	    has or should have, so they moved into the pinned files (two into `prose.md`, one into
140	    `versioning.md`, one into `AGENTS.md`) and two retired as answered
141	  - the sharpened convention behind it (wink): **intent decides the file, and nothing gates the
142	    edit**. A member writes a rule into its local pinned copy whenever it means the family to
143	    take it, without asking; `custom.md` is for what the member does *not* offer the family. The
144	    2026-08-05 entry below framed the same mechanism around experiments, which read as narrower

146	  - cost, and it is the same one the 2026-08-05 entry recorded: our pinned files now hold more
147	    unreviewed text than before, and nothing at acquaint shows a reader which parts the family

149	
150	- 2026-08-05 (`proposed`): a step is a title; the version and the step number both leave the prose
151	  record
152	  - the version was a second identifier for a step, and any prose naming one could be invalidated
153	    by a history rewrite. This repo's 2026-08-01 renumber is the evidence: it left transcripts and
154	    pasted reports that only the decoder entry below can read

171	  - a topic bookmark is a draft until it lands, so keeping its ladder self-consistent may rewrite

# custom-family.md - iiac-perf's layer, as a member of the vc-x1 agent-file family

Read after [custom.md](custom.md), whose single convention entry points here. Present only in a
member repo; a project that is not a member does not carry this file, and nothing in it applies to
one.

**A member's `custom.md` differs from the payload by that one line, and everything of its own lives
here.** That is the family's convention and it buys a property worth having: `diff custom.md
<template>/work/custom.md` is one line for every member, so the file that can never be pinned still
converges, and a member's whole customization surface is this file. The medium below is here for
that reason rather than because it has anything to do with the family.

## Medium and validation

The artifact is the `iiac-perf` CLI, a Rust crate (manifest `Cargo.toml`, package name
`iiac-perf`); versioning specifics in [versioning.md](agent-data/versioning.md).

**What a version bump promises**: nothing to a dependent, because there are none. `iiac-perf` is
a binary crate with no library target and no external consumers, so `X.Y.Z` is a scope signal to
readers of the history (see
[Advancing X.Y.Z](agent-data/versioning.md#advancing-xyz-scope-decides)) and not a compatibility
contract. Revisit with a compat clause if a library crate ever splits out.

- **Full validation**
  - when: per-commit checklist step 5
  - run as separate invocations, each exit status checked:
    1. `cargo fmt`
    2. `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`
    3. `cargo test`
    4. `cargo install --path . --locked`
    5. (re-test if anything substantive changed)
- **Fast validation**
  - when: ladder checklist step 3
  - `cargo test --bins`

The commands are the project's; the rule that each invocation's exit status is checked is
universal and lives in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md#working-practices).

## Membership

- **member name**: `iiac-perf`
- **template repository**: `../vc-x1-template`

These two are environment rather than instruction, the same species as `.vc-config.toml`'s
`[repos]` paths, and they belong there instead. They cannot move yet: `vc-x1 config --validate`
rejects keys it does not know (measured on 0.78.4, 2026-08-07), so a config carrying them would
fail its own validator.

## Messaging

Members leave word for each other in per-member mailboxes at the template repository. The protocol
is `../vc-x1-template/MESSAGES.md` and it governs; these are the parts that decide how a session
behaves.

- **At acquaint, check `../vc-x1-template/messages/iiac-perf.md`**; an absent file means no mail.
- **Handle, then delete** the entry, and delete the file once it empties. Mailboxes hold open items
  only.
- **So a message can never be a record.** Anything in one worth keeping is copied into
  `notes/chores/chores-NN.md` *before* the entry is deleted. Learned 2026-08-05, when a
  convergence message carried measurements that would have been lost with it.
- **Messages are thin pointers, not state.** Durable coordination state lives in topical files; a
  message says "action needed, see <file>" rather than restating the details.
- **Write to a member's mailbox, never into their repo.** A repo with a live session is written
  only by its own agent.

## Dogfood log

Dated entries on what this project is trying and where the pinned instructions chafed, failed, or
got amended; the evidence base for the family's convergence decisions
([Changing the agent-files](AGENTS.md#changing-the-agent-files)).

Each entry carries a **status**: `proposed` (in our agent-files, awaiting the family),
`adopted family-wide`, `rejected`, or `permanently local`. In-flight entries only: on
resolution an entry retires to [done.md](notes/done.md) with its narrative in
`notes/chores/chores-NN.md`, adopted and rejected alike. Entries predating the status
convention keep their form until touched.

- 2026-08-12 (`proposed`): validation runs at every commit, and the notes-only skip goes
  - the per-commit checklist stamped the version-of-record at step 4 and let step 5 be skipped
    for notes-only commits, so a commit could carry a version that no build ever had. Measured
    the same day: 0.24.5 and 0.24.6 both stamped and neither built, and `-V` answered 0.24.4
    until the next close-out jumped it three
  - wink's rule and his reason: every commit bumps the version precisely so a build exists
    carrying it, which makes an unbuilt bump a version nobody can run and the banner a claim
    nobody checked
  - so the skip goes at all three sites, and the step is conditioned on the medium rather than on
    the commit: run the artifact if the medium has one to run (wink). A first draft made the
    escape "too costly to build", which asks every project to judge its own cost and would be
    claimed by anyone who found validation tedious
  - each of the three sites gets one job so the rule is written once (wink): the checklist
    instructs, the protocol holds the reason and the medium condition, and `custom.md` holds the
    commands. A first pass had the checklist and the protocol carrying the same sentence
  - the same pass fixed a step number this morning's sync left stale, and dropped a
    cycle-at-a-glance clause that named validation as a close-out specialty. The stale number is
    the argument in miniature: it was a restatement, which is what let it drift unnoticed
  - rationale in [chores-06](notes/chores/chores-06.md#docs-validate-every-commit)

- 2026-08-07 (`proposed`): the family layer splits out of `custom.md`
  - `custom.md` had been accumulating things that only make sense because this repo belongs to a
    family: a member name, a template path, and a dogfood log whose status vocabulary reads
    `adopted family-wide`. wink's test is that `custom.md` should be usable as-is by a project that
    has never heard of us, and it failed that test
  - so the family layer moves here, and `custom.md` shrinks to a stub with nothing to substitute:
    a title naming no project, and one section. A member's copy differs from the payload's by the
    single conventions entry that points here, so `diff custom.md <template>/work/custom.md` is one
    line for every member
  - the pointer is that entry rather than an intro sentence (wink). We argued for the intro, on the
    grounds that four members carrying an identical one-line diff looks like a fake divergence; the
    answer is that it is a real project convention, and one line is cheaper than a paragraph every
    member has to keep in sync
  - the chain is `AGENTS.md` -> `custom.md` -> here, all of it prose, which is what lets the pinned
    set stay ignorant of the split. A non-member has no entry and no file
  - `CLAUDE.md` collapses to one line, `@AGENTS.md` (wink). It had grown a second `@` import per
    layer, which made it a second statement of what to read and therefore a second thing to keep
    true. Now `AGENTS.md` is the only source of that truth, and `CLAUDE.md` is payload-identical for
    every project, member or not. The cost is real and worth stating: nothing below `AGENTS.md` is
    auto-loaded any more, so hard rule 0 is load-bearing rather than a formality
  - one consequence needs the family's agreement, not ours: **"Check the mailbox at acquaint" leaves
    the pinned `AGENTS.md`** and lands in `## Messaging` above. vc-x1 pinned it in the 20260802
    snapshot, so this is a reversal. The argument is that a non-member cannot perform it at all,
    since building the mailbox path needs a member name and a template path they do not have, so it
    is dead text naming concepts they lack rather than a harmless no-op
  - deliberately not opened in the same pass: `AGENTS.md` still says "the family" and "member" where
    the generic mechanism is "the template payload and my copy of it". Same inconsistency one level
    up, and folding it in would roughly double the review surface of an already large configuration

- 2026-08-07 (`proposed`): cycles run on a bookmark, and `custom.md` stops holding rules
  - the bookmark rule had been adopted in principle since 2026-08-01 and was written down
    nowhere: `TODO.md` carried the intention, `cycle.md` said what a topic bookmark *is* once you
    have one, and neither creating nor landing one appeared in any agent-file. Two cycles ran on
    bookmarks anyway, on undocumented habit
  - so hard rule 13 states it, `cycle.md` gains an opening checklist and a land step, and
    `jj.md` gains the commands. Landing turns out to be the interesting half: it is the moment
    the cycle's commits become permanent, which makes it the trigger for the chores backfill
    that waits on permanence. That connection existed and had no owner
  - the create and land *commands* are deliberately separable from the rule, because wink
    expects a `vc-x1 start-change <bookmark>` to own the create half eventually
  - same pass, `custom.md` empties of conventions. Five entries were rules the family already
    has or should have, so they moved into the pinned files (two into `prose.md`, one into
    `versioning.md`, one into `AGENTS.md`) and two retired as answered
  - the sharpened convention behind it (wink): **intent decides the file, and nothing gates the
    edit**. A member writes a rule into its local pinned copy whenever it means the family to
    take it, without asking; `custom.md` is for what the member does *not* offer the family. The
    2026-08-05 entry below framed the same mechanism around experiments, which read as narrower
    than it is
  - cost, and it is the same one the 2026-08-05 entry recorded: our pinned files now hold more
    unreviewed text than before, and nothing at acquaint shows a reader which parts the family
    has agreed to. The diff is the answer and reading it is still manual

- 2026-08-05 (`proposed`): a step is a title; the version and the step number both leave the prose
  record
  - the version was a second identifier for a step, and any prose naming one could be invalidated
    by a history rewrite. This repo's 2026-08-01 renumber is the evidence: it left transcripts and
    pasted reports that only the decoder entry below can read
  - so the title becomes the identifier, a ladder rung carries neither a number nor a version, and
    the version-of-record is a build stamp living only in `Cargo.toml`. Every step still bumps it
  - the step number went too (wink): a rung sits in an ordered list, so a number beside it restates
    the position and then has to be maintained. Nothing renumbers, and a title need only be
    unambiguous within its cycle and within its chores file, where it is also an anchor
  - one exception, the chores as-built rung (wink): it records the version a *landed* commit
    carried, beside that commit's SHA, so the pair decodes an old `-V` banner. It takes the SHA's
    timing exactly, so an unlanded rung carries neither and a rebase cannot falsify a ladder
  - commit bodies tighten with it: a problem statement then a solution statement, both broad, with
    no file list, since the diff is already the mechanical record. The deliberation stays in
    chores, todo, and the session the `ochid:` trailer names, which is what the dual-repo model
    is for
  - that rule also took two passes. The first kept the body an edit list at one bullet per distinct
    change and survived one use, since writing this commit's own description produced thirteen
    bullets restating `git show --stat`. Clearing it exposed four contradictions of our own,
    including a title limit that read 50 in the authority file and 72 in three others
  - a topic bookmark is a draft until it lands, so keeping its ladder self-consistent may rewrite
    unlanded rungs; the exceptions are named rather than judged case by case
  - first cost measured, on this step itself: the version had been doubling as the eye's landmark
    in `## Done`, so removing it made the section hard to skim. `## Done` entries became a bold
    title plus sub-bullets, which is what `prose.md` had asked for all along and the version had
    been masking. We think other members will hit this wherever a long body hangs off a title in a
    flat list. Superseded in part 2026-08-07: vc-x1 wanted the version greppable, and the form is
    now the version ahead of the bold title, which serves both
  - drafted before the `measure-reproducibility` rebase so the cycle dogfoods it, per
    [Changing the agent-files](AGENTS.md#changing-the-agent-files); rationale in
    [chores-06](notes/chores/chores-06.md#docs-steps-are-titles-versions-are-stamps)

- 2026-08-05 (`proposed`): experiments move into the local agent-files, and `custom.md` narrows
  to what cannot be family-wide (superseded in scope by the 2026-08-07 entry above, which drops
  "experiment" for "anything the member offers the family")
  - the old rule sent every proposal to `custom.md` as an override, which made `custom.md` the
    staging area and guaranteed it grew non-generic, while the shared payload was the only place
    two members could collide
  - now the diff against the payload is the live proposal set and the commit history is the
    durable one, so neither has to be maintained by hand
  - the cost, recorded because it is real: a local agent-file no longer reads as family-agreed
    the way the payload does. We think an acquaint-time diff is the fix, and it is unbuilt
  - rationale in [chores-06](notes/chores/chores-06.md#docs-experiment-in-the-local-agent-files)
  - same session's family-convergence findings, kept in chores because the mailbox protocol is
    handle-then-delete, so a message can never be a record:
    - [jj revset primer audit](notes/chores/chores-06.md#jj-revset-primer-audit-2026-08-05): the
      payload's range bullets are wrong, and the error is the framing, not the gloss
    - [convergence measurements and positions](notes/chores/chores-06.md#convergence-measurements-and-positions-2026-08-05)

- 2026-08-02 (`proposed`): prose.md's <=100 wrap got misapplied as ~64 to match older files' look
  - the rule needed no change, the application did: surrounding narrow wrap is not a reason to
    wrap narrow, and one fact per sub-bullet beats a paragraph packing several (wink, reviewing
    TODO/chores additions)
  - extended to code comments at wink's direction
  - the application now lives in [prose.md](agent-data/prose.md#prose-form) itself, moved there
    2026-08-07; this entry stays until the family takes it

- 2026-08-01: published history renumbered under the new scope-based advancement rule
  - mapping: 0.24.0 -> 0.23.2 (grade-block compaction: presentation within the existing
    shape), 0.24.1 -> 0.23.3 (report docs), and the punctuation sweep lands as 0.23.4;

  - executed as a jj history rewrite of the two published commits (version-of-record and

the picked-up `## Todo` item **moves** here (never copied, one home per text) and becomes six
provisional items, all required, all revised as steps land. At close-out the whole block moves
into `notes/chores/chores-NN.md` and becomes that cycle's `##` section. It is never written in
two places. Shape:

```
### <type>: <title>

#### Problem
<what is wrong, a sentence or two>

#### Solution
<what will be done about it, broad; provisional until the close-out>

#### Acceptance check
<the measure of "are you finished?">

#### Ladder
- [[N]] [<cycle title> opening][M] (done)
- [[N]] [<title>][M] (current)
- [[N]] [<title>][M]
- [[N]] <cycle title> closing

#### Deliberation
<how the five above were decided; `_None._` if there was nothing to deliberate>

#### Ladder details
<one `#####` subsection per rung, headed by its exact title, opened at laddering with the
rung's intent and completed at landing with the conceptual delta; the closing rung's only at
close-out, gotchas in problem/solution form>

and the six items sit one level below that (headings give the current work durable anchors,
which numbered Todo entries can't). Full rules in
[cycle-protocol.md](agent-data/cycle-protocol.md#preparation); the move's four transforms are
in [Chores sections](agent-data/cycle-protocol.md#chores-sections).

_No cycle currently in progress._

## Todo

Entries are in **strict priority rank**, #1 highest, descending. Reprioritize by moving an
entry, then `vc-x1 fix-todo --no-dry-run TODO.md` to renumber. The numbers are positional rank,
not stable IDs. To refer to a Todo, name it by its **title** (a greppable mention; a numbered
list item has no anchor to link to), not its number. Long-tail entries live in
[todo-backlog.md](notes/todo-backlog.md). Use the

39	  choose their own persistence policy without endangering anything.

- **Records, not a positional line.** The line format was revised four times in about an hour,
  which is a format asking to become named fields. A `##` heading gives each record an anchor for
  free, so a reply can cite an exact entry with no invented id.
- **The remote reference is a commit permalink**, since a branch name rots exactly when the
  message becomes worth reading: a topic bookmark is deleted at landing and the permanent branch
  does not carry the file until then. That creates an ordering constraint the README now states,
  because a permalink cannot be written before the commit it names is pushed.
- **Strict for writers, tolerant for readers.** A malformed record is not an error, with one
  exception: the `##` heading must exist, because orphaned field lines join the record above, so
  an interrupted write damages its neighbour rather than itself.
- **Deliberately unsolved: notification.** No file in any repo can reach someone who is not
  looking. GitHub issues would, at the cost of moving correspondence outside the clone, the diff
  and jj history, so they are held in reserve for that one job.
- **Open for vc-x1**: whether a member's file may be created by whoever writes first, which is
  what a first message to a new member requires and which the README carries as a proposal rather
  than a rule.

### The specimen is the point of `messages/test-msg.md`

The one file this cycle adds to this repo is a two-line message. It exists so the README's
examples reference something real: a `local` path that resolves in a sibling clone and a `remote`
permalink that resolves for a reader with none.

**It also proves the ordering rule by needing it.** The README's permalinks pointed at a commit
that did not contain this file, so they answered 404 until it was committed and pushed. The rule
was written from that failure rather than in anticipation of it.

### Where this leaves the messages repo

`vc-x1-messages` is committed separately and is not part of this repo's history. This section is
the durable record of the reasoning, reachable from this commit's `ochid:` trailer, because a
plain repo has no agent repo of its own and its commits carry no trailer.

and whatever the review changes.

129	### Semicolons
130	
131	A semicolon earns its place only between equals: two parallel claims of the same weight, where
132	the contrast is the point ("The diff empties; the history keeps the record"). Everything else
133	that reaches for one is a structure decision not yet made. Make the decision:
134	
135	- **Item plus detail** (`claim; elaboration`): a detail worth keeping gets its own sentence, or
136	  its own sub-bullet where a reader skimming the list will actually notice it. A mere
137	  continuation of the thought takes a comma with a conjunction.
138	- **A list hiding in prose** (`A; B; C` inside a bullet): break the clauses into sub-bullets so
139	  the structure shows.
140	- **Legitimate besides the antithesis**: a semicolon separating list items that themselves
141	  contain commas; and semicolons inside code spans, which are syntax, not prose.
142	
143	Running prose is held to the same test, just less strictly: a sentence-join in an intro
144	paragraph is fine when both halves would stand as sentences and neither is a detail of the
145	other.
146	
147	### Typeable punctuation only
148	
149	Durable text uses punctuation that can be typed at a terminal. The prohibition is on
150	*authoring*, not presence: a file may legitimately hold a banned character it transcribed (see
151	below), so a byte scan is not the rule and a sweep needs the authored/transcribed judgment.
152	Banned from authoring: `—`, `–`, `…`, `→`. None can be entered without a compose key or a
153	paste, so none can be grepped for, and an em dash next to option syntax reads as another flag.
154	Unlike the semicolon rule above this one is absolute: they cost nothing to write and are paid on
155	every read, so a soft rule accumulates them.
156	
157	`…` becomes `...` and `→` becomes `->`. The dashes have no single replacement, because an em
158	dash usually stands in for a structural decision that was not made. Make the decision:
159	
160	- **A bullet's title and its body sharing a line** is a heading and a paragraph. Make the body
161	  sub-bullets.
162	- **A term and its definition** (`jj diff`, `<base>`, a flag) takes a colon, which keeps a
163	  glossary or a command list at one line per entry.

### Semicolons

A semicolon earns its place only between equals: two parallel claims of the same weight, where
the contrast is the point ("The diff empties; the history keeps the record"). Everything else
that reaches for one is a structure decision not yet made. Make the decision:

- **Item plus detail** (`claim; elaboration`): a detail worth keeping gets its own sentence, or
  its own sub-bullet where a reader skimming the list will actually notice it. A mere
  continuation of the thought takes a comma with a conjunction.
- **A list hiding in prose** (`A; B; C` inside a bullet): break the clauses into sub-bullets so
  the structure shows.
- **Legitimate besides the antithesis**: a semicolon separating list items that themselves
  contain commas; and semicolons inside code spans, which are syntax, not prose.

Running prose is held to the same test, just less strictly: a sentence-join in an intro
paragraph is fine when both halves would stand as sentences and neither is a detail of the
other.

### Typeable punctuation only

Durable text uses punctuation that can be typed at a terminal. The prohibition is on
*authoring*, not presence: a file may legitimately hold a banned character it transcribed (see
below), so a byte scan is not the rule and a sweep needs the authored/transcribed judgment.
Banned from authoring: `—`, `–`, `…`, `→`. None can be entered without a compose key or a
paste, so none can be grepped for, and an em dash next to option syntax reads as another flag.
Unlike the semicolon rule above this one is absolute: they cost nothing to write and are paid on
every read, so a soft rule accumulates them.

`…` becomes `...` and `→` becomes `->`. The dashes have no single replacement, because an em
dash usually stands in for a structural decision that was not made. Make the decision:

- **A bullet's title and its body sharing a line** is a heading and a paragraph. Make the body
  sub-bullets.
- **A term and its definition** (`jj diff`, `<base>`, a flag) takes a colon, which keeps a
  glossary or a command list at one line per entry.

content.text:
Both checks done. Here's what I found and what I think.

**The diff: confirmed, exactly two files, three hunks, all one proposal.** `AGENTS.md`, `custom.md`, and six of the eight `agent-data/` files are byte-identical to vc-x1's. The differences are `cycle-checklists.md` (2 hunks) and `cycle-protocol.md` (1 hunk), and all three hunks are the same thing: our 0.24.8 "validate every commit" rule, where their copies still allow the notes-only skip that produced the unbuilt 0.24.5/0.24.6 versions. This matches the open cycle's acceptance check word for word ("two files and three hunks, all of them 0.24.8's validation rule"), so the review rung can be written against a stable, minimal base. The review's verdict list is short: one proposal of ours to offer, zero differences of theirs to take.

**The semicolons: this is a rule change, not just a cleanup.** The wrinkle is that vc-x1 *pinned* a `Semicolons` rule in `prose.md` (identical in our copy) whose core is an allowance: a semicolon "earns its place between equals" ("The diff empties; the history keeps the record"), and their ~140-join sweep converted everything *except* those. What you're asking removes exactly the blessed case. So this isn't a sweep under the existing rule; it's tightening the rule to near-absolute, then sweeping. Three thoughts on that:

- **The argument for it is already sitting in the file.** The very next section, typeable punctuation, says "Unlike the semicolon rule above this one is absolute... a soft rule accumulates them." The current semicolon rule demands an equals-or-not judgment at every site, and judgment rules drift; an absolute rule is checkable with a grep (modulo code spans, which are syntax and stay). That's a clean family-facing rationale, and that contrast sentence would itself need editing as part of the change.
- **Scale is modest.** Roughly 50 prose semicolon sites across the pinned set (heaviest: `cycle-protocol.md` at 17, `prose.md` at 12), plus 35 in `custom-family.md`, which is ours alone and needs no family agreement. Most are the "equals" joins, which split naturally at a period ("Amend content; never re-describe" becomes two sentences). A handful are lists-in-prose that want sub-bullets, e.g. the rewrite-exceptions clause that appears in both checklist and protocol. The `Semicolons` section itself needs rewriting rather than sweeping, since its examples demonstrate the allowance being removed.
- **Sequencing matters, and I'd review first, sweep second.** Sweeping now would turn today's three-hunk diff into edits across nearly every pinned file, right when the review rung's job is to name every difference with a verdict. Better: write the review against the clean base, carry the semicolon tightening in the reply as a proposal (per rule 12 it eventually lands as an edit to pinned `prose.md` plus the sweep), and run the sweep as its own small cycle — "convention work runs as its own cycle" says exactly this, and vc-x1 set the precedent themselves with "review the rule, not each instance." The `custom-family.md` sweep could ride along any time, since it's not pinned.

One boundary question worth deciding before the sweep: whether the rule stays scoped to prose (semicolons in code spans and code examples are syntax and untouched) — I'd assume yes, and the current rule's other carve-out, semicolons separating comma-bearing list items, presumably converts to bullets under your formulation.

The plain version: our set and vc-x1's now differ only by our one validation-rule proposal, so the owed review is small and clean. The semicolon removal is really a tightening of a rule vc-x1 just pinned, so I'd propose it to them in the review reply rather than sweeping first, then do the sweep as its own cycle once they've seen it — that keeps the review's diff readable and gives the family one rule to judge instead of fifty edits.

~125 comment lines in `src/` also carry semicolons — that matters for the rule's scope, so the plan below accounts for it. Here's the plan, for your review before I touch anything.

## Plan: cycle "docs: semicolons leave the agent-files"

Own convention cycle on a topic bookmark off `main` (0.24.10), slug-named per rule 13. Multi-step: two rungs plus close-out, versions 0.24.11-0, 0.24.11-1, closing 0.24.11 (patch scope: prose within the existing shape). Ladder:

1. **Opening** — bookmark, In Progress block, version bump.
2. **Rung 1: modify the semicolon rule in prose.md** (its own commit, so the proposal reads alone in history):
   - Rewrite `### Semicolons`: in **code and agent-files (including custom\*)**, authored prose carries no semicolons. Every site converts: a period when the halves are two claims, a comma with a conjunction when one continues the other, sub-bullets when a list is hiding in prose. Semicolons inside code spans and fenced code stay — they're syntax.
   - **Historical exemption, scoped**: all other durable text (notes/, chores, README, TODO) keeps its existing semicolons for now, converting when touched. The rule states both halves explicitly.
   - Record the why: the "between equals" allowance requires a judgment at every site, and agents take advantage of the exceptions — each site's author judges in their own favor. An absolute-within-scope rule needs no judgment and is nearly greppable. (This mirrors the typeable-punctuation section's own rationale.)
   - Fix the knock-ons in the same file: the section's examples currently demonstrate the removed allowance, and the next section's contrast sentence ("Unlike the semicolon rule above this one is absolute") now contrasts scope, not softness.

3. **Rung 2: sweep the agent-files** — hand-judged conversions, not sed, across `AGENTS.md` (6 sites), `custom-family.md` (35), `agent-data/*` (~61 raw, prose.md's rule section already done in rung 1). Verification: a check that blanks fenced blocks and backtick spans, then asserts zero `;` remaining per file — the check and its output go in the record. Full cargo validation per commit as usual.
4. **Close-out** — records move to chores, land on `main`, delete the bookmark.

**After landing** (not in the ladder): the proposal message to vc-x1 goes in `../vc-x1-messages/vc-x1.md` under their accepted protocol — a record pointing at the two landed commits and the chores section, with their own line back to them: review the rule, not each instance.

Two things I need your call on:

- **The `src/` comments.** Your rule says historical semicolons are *not* OK in code, and there are ~125 comment lines carrying them. I recommend that sweep be its own follow-up cycle (it's twice the size of this one and touches every doc comment), with a ranked Todo entry created at this cycle's close-out — the rule lands now, the code sweep follows named. Say if you'd rather have it as a third rung here.
- **Ordering vs the open convergence cycle.** Both this cycle and the convergence bookmark's pending review rung will edit TODO.md, chores-07, and Cargo.toml, so whichever lands second rebases through conflicts. I'd land this cycle first and write the formal review afterward against the post-sweep files, folding this proposal into the full reply — which matches your "implement, then propose" sequencing anyway.

The plain version: one new cycle, two commits — first the rule change, then the sweep of ~100 semicolon sites in the agent-files — then land it and tell vc-x1 to review the rule rather than the edits. The only open choices are whether the code-comment sweep is a third rung or its own next cycle (I say next cycle), and confirming this lands before the convergence review gets written.

1	# Cycle checklists
2	
3	Checklists for the moments where slips happen: committing, pushing, closing out. The full
4	protocol, with rationale and recovery procedures, is
5	[cycle-protocol.md](cycle-protocol.md). On any disagreement, that file wins. Re-read
6	the relevant checklist immediately before the action. Don't run it from memory.
7	
8	Universal file, shared with the template repository. A proposed change is edited here and
9	converges at the template ([Changing the agent-files](../AGENTS.md#changing-the-agent-files)).
10	Project-local content goes in [custom.md](../custom.md).
11	
12	## The cycle at a glance
13	
14	Every change runs as a **cycle** with three phases: Preparation -> Work -> Close-out. The
15	phases always happen, but there are two styles. A **multi-step** cycle commits them
16	individually, as a ladder of steps (the Preparation commit is optional); a
17	**single-step** cycle folds all three into one commit when the change is straightforward, so
18	that one commit is the close-out and carries its duties. So a
19	single-step cycle is one commit, and a multi-step is minimum two (a Work commit plus the
20	close-out), typically three or more (the definition is
21	[AGENTS.md's Terminology](../AGENTS.md#terminology)). The
22	ladder lists a cycle's steps in order and identifies each by its title, with no number and no
23	version. Where the version-of-record lives and how often it is bumped are in
24	[versioning.md](versioning.md). Read [cycle-protocol.md](cycle-protocol.md) before any commit
25	work, and before any push, cycle or not.
26	
27	## Cycles run on a bookmark
28	
29	A cycle runs on one topic bookmark in the work repo, created at the opening and named by the
30	cycle title's slug (the anchor algorithm in
31	[Markdown anchor links](notes.md#markdown-anchor-links)). `main` advances only when the
32	finished cycle lands on it; nothing pushes straight to `main`. The bot repo needs no bookmark:
33	its `main` rides the tip of its linear narrative.
34	
35	- **The bookmark is the unit of review.** Everything the cycle does is visible as one line
36	  against `main`, and until it lands the whole line is a draft that can be reshaped
37	  ([Topic bookmarks are drafts](#topic-bookmarks-are-drafts)). Landing is the single approval
38	  that makes the cycle permanent.
39	- **Create at the opening**, land at the close-out. Commands are in
40	  [Cycle bookmarks](jj.md#cycle-bookmarks-create-and-land), and the opening's other duties are in
41	  the [Opening checklist](#opening-checklist) below.
42	- **A single-step cycle still gets one.** The saving is not worth the exception, and a
43	  one-commit line is exactly the case where a pre-landing rewrite is cheapest.
44	- **The permanent branch is whatever this project calls it** (`main` here). A long-lived program
45	  bookmark is a different animal, governed by
46	  [Long-lived bookmarks](jj.md#long-lived-bookmarks-merge-only-by-default-deletable-once-merged).
47	
48	**Why:** a cycle that pushes `main` directly makes every correction a coordinated force-push of
49	published history. Landing costs one command and buys free rewrites for the whole cycle.
50	
51	## Opening checklist
52	
53	At the cycle's opening, before the first Work commit:
54	
55	1. Create the cycle's bookmark ([Cycle bookmarks](jj.md#cycle-bookmarks-create-and-land)).
56	2. Move the picked-up item into `TODO.md > ## In Progress` and write the **six provisional
57	   items** there, all six required. The title is a heading one level below `## In Progress`'s
58	   own level, and the other five are headings one level below the title (a plain cycle: `###`
59	   title, `####` items; under a program heading, each one deeper):
60	   - **title**, which becomes the chores section header at close-out
61	   - **problem statement**: what is wrong, a sentence or two
62	   - **solution statement**: what will be done about it, broad
63	   - **acceptance check**: the measure of "are you finished?"
64	   - **ladder**: one rung per step, `- [[N]] [<title>][M]` plus `(current)` / `(done)`, with
65	     `[M]: #<slug>` in the file's `# References` (the closing rung, `<cycle title> closing`,
66	     unlinked until its gotchas subsection exists)
67	   - **deliberation**: how the five above were decided (`_None._` when there was nothing to
68	     deliberate)
69	   A `Ladder details` area follows the six: one subsection per rung, headed by the rung's
70	   exact title, opened at laddering with the rung's intent and completed as rungs land; the
71	   closing rung's is created at close-out only if gotchas occurred (see the protocol's
72	   [Preparation](cycle-protocol.md#preparation)).
73	3. Sweep `## Done` per [Retiring Done entries](notes.md#retiring-done-entries), then bump the
74	   version-of-record.
75	
76	Nothing is opened in the chores file here. The block is the cycle's only home until close-out
77	moves it. See [Chores sections](cycle-protocol.md#chores-sections).
78	
79	**Why the acceptance check:** a cycle's own checklists are per-commit instruments and every one
80	of them can pass while the banner claim is false. Measured in a seven-cycle program opened
81	against "end subprocess spawning": its close-out claimed the goal met, with about twenty spawn
82	sites surviving, two inside the facade the program built. A measurement or performance claim is
83	the shape most exposed, since "we measured it" is easy to believe and hard to notice you have not
84	done. Being provisional, the check can also be revised *toward* what was achieved, which is the
85	same failure by a slower route. A changed check is one of the things the deliberation justifies.
86	
87	## Committing vs pushing
88	
89	A cycle rung is committed *by* `vc-x1 push`. Never pre-commit it with `jj commit`. Push's
90	commit stages commit both repos with the approved title/body and stamp each new commit's
91	`ochid:` trailer (see [ochid trailers](jj.md#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers)). A
92	pre-committed rung leaves `@` empty and push mints a stamped empty duplicate. In
93	an instruction, "commit", "push", and "commit + push" all mean `vc-x1 push`. A bare `jj commit`
94	is asked for by name ("local commit", "just `jj commit`") and is only for work that never
95	publishes (local-only saves and loop-and-squash intermediates), with no `ochid:`. The approval
96	around a push, interactive by default and waived only by an explicit scoped delegation, is the
97	cycle protocol's [Pushing policy](cycle-protocol.md#policy).
98	
99	## Topic bookmarks are drafts
100	
101	A topic bookmark is a draft until it lands on a permanent branch. Pushed there is not published.
102	So keep the series inside it self-consistent: inserting or reordering a step edits the ladder in
103	the rungs that already committed an older version of it, not only at the tip.
104	
105	- **Amend content, never re-describe.** Editing `TODO.md` in a rung and amending is not a
106	  `jj describe`, so hard rule 4 stays intact and the `ochid:` trailers ride along untouched
107	  (they carry change ids, which survive a rewrite).
108	- **Then force-push the bookmark**, under the same approval as any other push.
109	- **Exceptions, where self-consistency is not worth its cost**: the bookmark has already landed;
110	  another branch is stacked on it, so the rewrite becomes someone else's rebase; or the ladder
111	  is long and only a trailing snapshot disagrees.
112	
113	The squash-form ladder below never meets this, since nothing on it is pushed. The rule is for the
114	multi-commit shape, whose rungs publish one at a time. Full statement in the protocol's
115	[Topic bookmarks are drafts](cycle-protocol.md#topic-bookmarks-are-drafts).
116	
117	## Per-commit checklist
118	
119	Every commit (Preparation, each Work commit, Close-out), per the protocol's
120	[Per-commit flow](cycle-protocol.md#per-commit-flow):
121	
122	1. Mark the rung `(current)` in `TODO.md > ## In Progress`, as the first edit.
123	2. Do the work. On any deviation from the agreed plan, or any question, stop and surface it.
124	3. Flip `(current)` -> `(done)`, before validation and the commit, and complete the rung's
125	   `Ladder details` subsection with the conceptual delta (its intent stub was opened when the
126	   rung was laddered; the ladder itself stays a bare ToC). See the protocol's
127	   [Preparation](cycle-protocol.md#preparation).
128	4. Bump the version-of-record to this commit's version (the suffix scheme is in
129	   [versioning.md](versioning.md)). The opening checklist's bump already covers a Preparation
130	   commit.
131	5. Validate the artifact at every commit, doc-only ones included. The medium's commands are in
132	   [custom.md](../custom.md).
133	6. Stop and ask the user, "please review", as this is the bottom of the review loop. Do not present
134	   a description as we iterate until the user reviews and says "continue|go|.." indicating the work
135	   review is likely complete.
136	7. Once the work review is complete, write the description: a conventional title, then a body in
137	   prose.md's [Commit-body form](prose.md#commit-body-form) (an intro paragraph stating the
138	   general problem, `*` bullets for its facets, `-` bullets for solutions, a `-` solving the
139	   nearest enclosing problem), sized per [Line widths](prose.md#line-widths). No version in
140	   either, no file list (the diff is the mechanical record), and no deliberation (chores, todo,
141	   and the session hold that). See [Commit description](cycle-protocol.md#commit-description).
142	8. Show title + body and stop for review. This review covers the push only when the user's go
143	   explicitly includes it.
144	9. On the user's go: `vc-x1 push <bookmark> --title "..." --body "..."`. Never pre-commit with
145	   `jj commit`; never hand-write `ochid:` trailers.
146	
147	## Ladder (sub-cycle) checklist
148	
149	Within a sub-cycle ladder, per the protocol's
150	[per-Work-commit contract](cycle-protocol.md#per-work-commit-contract-within-a-ladder):
151	
152	1. `jj new -R .`: fresh empty `@`.
153	2. Do the commit's work.
154	3. Run the fast validation (named in [custom.md](../custom.md)). Non-negotiable.
155	4. `jj describe -m "..." -m "..." -R .`: scratch working title. This first-time authoring is
156	   the one permitted describe. The commit is never published and never carries a trailer.
157	
158	Nothing on a ladder is pushed. The close-out squash
159	(`jj squash --from "<base>..@-" --into @ -u -R .`) collapses it, and `vc-x1 push` then
160	publishes the single commit.
161	
162	## Before any push
163	
164	- This specific push has the user's explicit approval. Approval of a plan that includes a push
165	  is not push approval. "Commit and push" names the destination, not a waiver of the reviews.
166	  Only an explicit scoped delegation ("do all of X, don't check in") waives the stops, for that
167	  bounded task only. Delegation waives stops, never flow (records, validation, the bookmark
168	  discipline; see the protocol's [Policy](cycle-protocol.md#policy)), and destructive ops
169	  still pause.
170	- Validation ran, and passed, after the last edit.
171	- Closing words are already written. Nothing follows the turn's final push (next checklist).
172	
173	## After the final push: hard stop
174	
175	Once the turn's final push or bot-repo squash-push is invoked, do no further work: no
176	verification, no summary, no next-step offers, no edits, until the user speaks. Put all closing
177	words *before* the invoke. The harness rejects an empty turn, so it may force a visible token
178	after the tool returns. If so, emit a bare acknowledgment only (e.g. "landed"), never a summary
179	or more work. Post-push verification happens next turn at the user's direction. A standing
180	delegation makes intermediate pushes just steps; the hard stop lands on the turn's *final*
181	push. See
182	[After push or squash-push](cycle-protocol.md#after-push-or-squash-push-stop-and-wait).
183	
184	## Close-out checklist
185	
186	The cycle's last step, per the protocol's
187	[Close-out](cycle-protocol.md#close-out):
188	
189	1. **Run the acceptance check** the opening stated, and record what it showed in the
190	   `## In Progress` block, whether or not it passed. A check that was never run is a failed
191	   close-out, and a check that failed is a finding, not a reason to quietly restate the banner.
192	2. **Finalize the six items in place**: sync the title if the scope shifted, replace the
193	   provisional solution statement with what was done, drop the ladder's `(current)` / `(done)`
194	   markers, add any design subsections, and write the closing rung's gotchas subsection
195	   (problem/solution form) if closing surfaced any.
196	3. **Move the block** into `notes/chores/chores-NN.md`, which is what creates the section.
197	   Four transforms, two of which fail silently: headings one level deeper, rung refs renumbered
198	   into the destination's namespace, repo-root-relative links gain `../`, forward-looking notes
199	   rewritten. See [Chores sections](cycle-protocol.md#chores-sections). Add the title-only
200	   `## Table of Contents` entry.
201	4. Write the `## Done` entry: the version, then a bold title line with its chores `[N]` ref,
202	   detail as sub-bullets (see [Done entry form](notes.md#done-entry-form)). Replace the
203	   `## In Progress` block with `_No cycle currently in progress._`.
204	5. Full validation, mandatory.
205	6. Update `notes/README.md` if functionality changed.
206	7. At push time, surface the shape options (squash / trapezoid / keep separate) and wait for
207	   the user's choice. The trapezoid recipe is
208	   [in the protocol](cycle-protocol.md#trapezoid-close-out-recipe). Its step 4 is
209	   `jj git push`, not `vc-x1 push`.
210	8. **Land the bookmark** on the user's go. Until this, nothing the cycle pushed is permanent.
211	   Once `main` contains the bookmark, delete it, locally and remotely. See
212	   [Cycle bookmarks](jj.md#cycle-bookmarks-create-and-land).
213	9. Backfill the chores as-built ladder refs (and any remaining legacy `Commits:` lines) for the
214	   commits landing just made permanent, which is the whole cycle rather than the previous push's
215	   share. Never record a SHA that is not on a permanent branch. The backfill edits ride the next
216	   push (a commit cannot record its own SHA).
217	
218	## vc-x1 push behaviors to keep in mind
219	
220	Three, independent of project language:
221	
222	- **No checks of the project's own.** vc-x1 assumes nothing about a repo's contents beyond
223	  `.jj` and `.vc-config.toml`, and runs no build or tests. The medium's validation is the
224	  per-commit flow's job, run *before* invoking `vc-x1 push`. The one check that remains is
225	  `push-work` verifying the bookmark's remote refs are tracked, which is its own precondition.
226	- **Rerunning is safe.** Push keeps no state and cannot resume. Every stage no-ops when its
227	  work is already done, so a failed run is re-run, not resumed. If a run fails, push stops and
228	  reports. Getting the repos back to a sensible state is the user's call, not something the
229	  tool infers.
230	- **ochid trailers** are injected by `vc-x1 push` itself, so don't hand-write them into the
231	  commit body or `--title`/`--body`.
