attachment.snippet:
1	# Prose and durable text
2	
3	How long-lived text is written on this project: the prose shape, the punctuation rules, and the
4	commit-title identity. Read this before writing durable text (notes files, commit messages, doc
5	comments, chores sections).
6	
7	Universal file, shared with the template repository. A proposed change is edited here and
8	converges at the template ([Changing the agent-files](../AGENTS.md#changing-the-agent-files)).
9	Project-local content goes in [custom.md](../custom.md).
10	
11	## Prose form
12	
13	Long-lived prose on this project follows one basic shape: a short intro that explains the *why*
14	or the high-level *what*, sharpened to a *problem statement* where a surface calls for one (see
15	[Problem-first shape](#problem-first-shape)), then a `-` bullet list for the details. The width
16	numbers and the wrap discipline live in [Line widths](#line-widths) below, their one home. One
17	fact per bullet or sub-bullet beats a paragraph packing several. Avoid wall-of-prose paragraphs:
18	they hide the structure that bullets make scannable. Punctuation that joins clauses without
19	naming their relationship is the same failure at sentence scale. See
20	[Semicolons](#semicolons) and
21	[Typeable punctuation only](#typeable-punctuation-only).
22	
23	Surfaces that use this shape:
24	
25	- Module / function / struct / field doc comments in `.rs` files. See
26	  [Doc comments](code.md#doc-comments-on-every-file-function-and-method).
27	- Commit message bodies (both work-repo and bot-repo). The title is the commit-specific
28	  add-on. See [Per-commit flow](cycle-protocol.md#per-commit-flow).
29	- Chore descriptions in `notes/chores/chores-NN.md`. See
30	  [Chores section content](notes.md#chores-section-content-no-edit-list-git-is-the-record).
31	- Todo entries in `TODO.md` when an entry needs more than one line of detail. Pure one-liners
32	  are still fine. Done entries take the same shape with the title bolded, detail always as
33	  sub-bullets rather than sentences trailing off the title line. See
34	  [Done entry form](notes.md#done-entry-form).
35	
36	Bullet *content* differs by surface:
37	
38	- **Commit bodies**: the [Problem-first shape](#problem-first-shape) for finished work, arranged
39	  by [Commit-body form](#commit-body-form) below. What is specific to a commit:
40	  - the problem statement defines any word the title assumes, since the title is what a reader
41	    meets first and it answers the problem
42	  - **no file list.** The diff and `git show --stat` are the mechanical record, so restating them
43	    is a second copy that can drift from the first. An import of a thousand files is one change
44	  - these are claims a reader has to follow, so they are sentences rather than fragments. A
45	    bullet wanting a paragraph belongs in the chores section instead
46	  - the **deliberation** stays out: alternatives weighed, evidence, dates, costs accepted. Those
47	    live in the chores section, the `## Todo` entry, and the session the `ochid:` trailer names,
48	    each reachable from the commit by construction. The problem itself is a *why* and belongs
49	    here
50	- **Chores / todo / done**: bullets are conceptual (design points, structural notes, the "what
51	  landed and why" at a notch above file-list granularity). Never a copy of the commit's edit
52	  list. See
53	  [Chores section content](notes.md#chores-section-content-no-edit-list-git-is-the-record).
54	- **Doc comments**: bullets are whatever structure fits (fields, cases, invariants).
55	
56	### Line widths
57	
58	Every width number lives here and nowhere else: the other files and sections link here rather
59	than restating one, so a change is a single edit and the copies cannot drift. Consolidated
60	2026-08-09, when the body width moved and the restatements had to be hunted.
61	
62	- **Prose**, all durable text: wrap at <=100 cols, bullet continuations indented two spaces.
63	- **Source**, doc comments and inline comments included: <=100 cols, which is rustfmt's default
64	  `max_width` (enforcement notes in [code.md](code.md#line-width)).
65	- **Commit titles**: <=50 chars.
66	- **Commit bodies**: <=75 cols, the Linux kernel patch standard. It replaced git's older 72
67	  convention here 2026-08-09, and published bodies keep the wrap they shipped with.
68	
69	The widths are wrap defaults, not absolutes (the title cap excepted). Existing text re-wraps
70	when touched, no mass sweeps. Write to the full width: wrap near the limit rather than
71	imitating the narrow wrap of older text, and a line that reads better long stays long (an URL,
72	a literal report row, indented code in a comment).
73	
74	### Problem-first shape
75	
76	`## In Progress` cycle blocks, chores sections, `## Todo` entries, and commit bodies use a sharper
77	form of the same shape: a problem, then how it is answered, then the steps that get there.
78	
79	- **Problem statement** (the why): one or two sentences. Don't pad with intent, don't restate
80	  what follows it.
81	- **Solution statement** (the what/how): what is done about the problem, in broad terms,
82	  answering whatever question the problem statement raises. Surface-specific rules are in
83	  [Bullet content differs by surface](#prose-form) above.
84	- **Plan bullets** (the what/when), the steps. Formality differs by surface:
85	  - In Progress / chores: a committed ladder, one step per commit. See
86	    [Conventional-commit shape](#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--chores--commit) for the
87	    per-step title + `(current)` / `(done)` form.
88	  - Todo entries: rough informal bullets, no numbering, formalized only when the entry is
89	    picked up into a cycle.
90	
91	**Timing decides whether the solution statement is provisional, not whether it is written.** A
92	cycle writes one at Preparation, before the work, and revises it as steps land. The close-out's
93	commit body carries the final one. A `## Todo` entry's is provisional in the same way. Only a
94	commit body's is settled, because a commit is finished by the time it has one. The earlier rule
95	here said a plan was for work not yet done and a solution for work that is, which left a cycle
96	unable to say at its opening what it intended to do.
97	
98	### Commit-body form
99	
100	A commit body is the [Problem-first shape](#problem-first-shape) with one addition: a body whose
101	problem has several sub-problems arranges them by a fixed recursion, so a reader knows what any
102	bullet is from its marker and its depth. The earlier statement, "a problem statement then a
103	solution statement, both broad", left that arrangement to taste, and taste converged slowly and
104	separately.
105	
106	- **An intro paragraph states the general problem**, and defines any word the title assumes. It
107	  is mandatory. [Prose form](#prose-form) wants it regardless, and a body opening on a bullet is

112	- **`-` bullets are solutions**, and a `-` solves the nearest enclosing problem: nested under a
113	  `*` facet it solves that facet, at top level it solves the intro's general problem, which is
114	  how one solution says it retires every facet at once. Position expresses scope.
115	- **Zero facets is the trivial commit**: a problem paragraph and one or more top-level `-`
116	  solutions. Not a second form, the general form with an empty middle.
117	
118	**The markers are typed on purpose**: `*` always means problem, `-` always means solution.
119	Indentation alone cannot separate them in the trivial case, where a lone top-level `-` reads as a
120	solution only because `-` always is one. The typing also keeps history greppable (`^\* ` finds
121	every facet, `^- ` and `^  - ` every solution). Bodies are read as plain text, in `jj log` and in

vc-x1-dev 0.78.8-8

Commit both repos, push the work repo's BOOKMARK, and
squash-push the bot repo's `main`: one command.

Collapses the manual commit-push-publish ceremony into a
single subcommand with two interactive approval gates.

Stages, in order:
  - review           approve the diff (first gate)
  - message          $EDITOR, or --title/--body; approve
                     the text (second gate). Skipped when
                     neither repo has pending changes
  - commit-work      commit the work repo. Skipped when
                     `@` is empty
  - commit-bot       commit `.claude`. Skipped when it is
                     clean
  - bookmark-set     work repo -> <bookmark>, bot -> main
  - push-work        publish <bookmark> to origin
  - squash-push-bot  fold `.claude`'s trailing writes
                     into its commit and push main

Rerunning is always safe: each stage does nothing when its
work is already done, so a failed run is re-run rather than
resumed. There is no saved state: vc-x1 cannot know why a
run failed, so it stops and reports. Please fix and try
again.

Failures in commit-work / commit-bot / bookmark-set roll both
repos back via `jj op restore` to a snapshot taken moments
earlier. Once push-work succeeds the work is published: from
there a change is either a new commit appended on top by the
next push, or an amend of what was pushed: `vc-x1
squash-push` folds the working copy into the last commit and
force-updates the remote.

vc-x1 runs no build or test steps: run your project's checks
yourself before pushing.

Non-interactive use: pass both --title and --body plus --yes
to skip both gates.

Usage: vc-x1-dev push [OPTIONS] [BOOKMARK]

Arguments:
  [BOOKMARK]
          Bookmark to advance in the work repo (positional form of
          `--bookmark`). The bot repo always advances `main`.
          
          Accepting a positional lets the common case read as `vc-x1 push main`
          without the `--bookmark` ceremony; `--bookmark` is kept as an alias
          for scripts and for composition with other args. The two forms
          conflict if both supplied.

Options:
      --bookmark <BOOKMARK>
          Bookmark to advance in the work repo (flag form; see positional)

  -V, --version...
          Version detail on stdout: -V the banner, -VV the full report (as
          `vc-x1 version`). Counted like -v/-vv.
          
          Both ride along: they print, then the subcommand runs, so one
          invocation captures the version and the command's output together.
          That is why this replaces clap's auto-version, which would exit after
          printing. Without either, the banner still prints, on stderr.

      --no-banner
          Suppress the banner stderr normally carries on every run.
          
          Only the ambient banner: an explicit `-V` still prints, since asking
          for it outranks suppressing it.

      --step
          Pause between every stage for an interactive approval gate

      --allow-jj-mismatch
          Run even when `jj -V` disagrees with our linked jj-lib.
          
          Per-invocation on purpose, never a config key: a key gets set once
          during a frustrating afternoon and then silently protects nothing.

      --no-squash-push
          Stop before `squash-push-bot` so it can be run manually

      --dry-run
          Print the exact commands for every stage without side effects

  -v, --verbose...
          Verbose output: -v debug, -vv trace

      --log <LOG>
          Log file path (captures all levels)

      --title <STR>
          Commit title (skip `$EDITOR` for the message stage)

      --body <STR>
          Commit body (skip `$EDITOR` for the message stage)

  -y, --yes
          Auto-approve interactive prompts (review gate, message-edit
          confirmation). Required when `--title` / `--body` aren't both supplied
          in non-interactive contexts

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

23	A shared repo for family correspondence, built in one sitting and unreviewed by anyone else. The
24	protocol lives in its own `README.md` at format 0.1.0, and this project's inbox is `iiac-perf.md`
25	beside it. What is recorded here is what was decided and why, since the README states the rules
26	without the alternatives they beat.
27	
28	The repo exists because the transport was the defect rather than the messages riding it. That
29	diagnosis came out of a day spent finding that everything owed to another member was sitting in a
30	gitignored scratch file, with no durable place to put it.
31	
32	- **Why a repo at all.** Mailboxes live in the template repository, whose `main` is a single
33	  `Initial commit` with everything else uncommitted, so a handled message deleted there is
34	  unrecoverable. `custom-family.md`'s copy-into-chores-before-deleting rule exists only to
35	  compensate for that.
36	- **Plain, with no agent, and the reason is structural rather than taste.** A managed repo
37	  inherits "a repo with a live session is written only by its own agent", which is the rule that
38	  created mailboxes in the first place, so a manager would make the one repo everyone must write
39	  to writable by one member. What replaces the manager is a rule: whoever writes a record commits
40	  it, in the same act.
41	- **Bodies stay in the sender's repo and only pointers live in the shared one.** That is what
42	  makes a notification record losable without loss, which in turn is what lets each file's owner
43	  choose their own persistence policy without endangering anything.
44	- **Records, not a positional line.** The line format was revised four times in about an hour,
45	  which is a format asking to become named fields. A `##` heading gives each record an anchor for
46	  free, so a reply can cite an exact entry with no invented id.
47	- **The remote reference is a commit permalink**, since a branch name rots exactly when the
48	  message becomes worth reading: a topic bookmark is deleted at landing and the permanent branch
49	  does not carry the file until then. That creates an ordering constraint the README now states,
50	  because a permalink cannot be written before the commit it names is pushed.
51	- **Strict for writers, tolerant for readers.** A malformed record is not an error, with one
52	  exception: the `##` heading must exist, because orphaned field lines join the record above, so
53	  an interrupted write damages its neighbour rather than itself.

Good moment to check rather than plow on. Assessment:

**These conflicts are the predicted ones, not a sign of damage.** The convergence cycle's deliberation recorded it in advance — "Both cycles edit `TODO.md`, `notes/chores/chores-07.md`, and `Cargo.toml`, so the conflict is known and accepted" — and you accepted "whichever lands second rebases" on exactly that basis. The rebase conflicted in precisely those files plus `Cargo.lock` (the version line's shadow), and nowhere else: no `agent-data/` file, nothing in `src/`. Each conflict is the expected shape — the version line (main says 0.25.1, the branch's opening stamped 0.24.10-0), and the records files where both lines appended different sections to the same spots. jj kept both sides intact, so nothing was lost.

**What "something bad" would look like**, and didn't happen: conflicts in files only one line should have touched (the pinned agent-files, source), or a side missing its content. If that ever shows up mid-rebase, the right move is not to resolve but to abort: `jj op log` to find the operation before the rebase, then `jj op restore <op>` — jj's operation log makes the whole rebase undoable in one step.

**What I was doing, and propose to continue**: resolve the four by hand on top of the conflicted opening, then `jj squash` the resolution into it (amend content, never re-describe — the trailer survives):

- `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock`: the cycle re-stamps on the new base as **0.25.2-0**, with the deliberation's "Patch scope, so 0.24.10-0" updated to match.
- `TODO.md`: the only conflict is the references block — main's `[93]`–`[95]` chores pointers versus the branch's two rung fragments. Keep main's three, renumber the block's rung refs to `[96]`–`[98]`, and while in there bring the block up to the new rules: link the closing rung, add its stub, absorb Todo #1 ("Converge agent-files with vc-x1") into the block per your plan, and refresh the stale acceptance-check numbers.
- `chores-07.md`: keep main's full file and re-apply the branch's addition (the convergence-findings section) in position — jj is showing that addition as a clean diff, so it's a mechanical replay.

content.text:
Agreed, and the miss is instructive: the conflicts *were* predicted — but the prediction lived in a record written days ago, not in the moment before the command ran. I knew the rebase would conflict in four files and ran it without saying so, so the wall of markers read as breakage to anyone watching, including a version of me with less context. The knowledge existing somewhere isn't the same as it being on the table when the scary output arrives.

So the practice I'd adopt, concretely: **before any command whose expected outcome is not clean** — a rebase across diverged lines, a force-push, a first run of a tool being dogfooded — say three things first: what output to expect (including "this will print conflict markers in these files"), what *unexpected* would look like, and the abort path (`jj op restore` for anything jj, rerun-is-safe for vc-x1 push). Then take the fixing one step at a time, each step small enough to check together. It's really the forward-looking half of rule 10: stop-and-ask covers surprises after they happen; this prevents an expected event from arriving as a surprise at all.

Two places it should live, and I'd do neither mid-cycle: it's family-shaped (nothing iiac-perf-specific about it), so per rule 12 it eventually belongs in a pinned file — probably AGENTS.md's working practices, near the one-command-per-invocation rule — via its own small convention cycle. Until then I'll simply practice it, and this conversation plus the cycle's records hold the why. I can also drop a one-line Todo so it doesn't evaporate.

Resuming the resolution your way, one step at a time. Step 1 is the smallest: `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock`, replacing the conflict block with `0.25.2-0` (the cycle re-stamped on its new base). Expected output: none — two quiet edits, verified by the next `cargo` run. Shall I?

  | After the final push | After push or squash-push: stop and wait |
  | Close-out checklist | Close-out |

  before acting; the checklist's own header says the protocol wins on any disagreement. So the file
  an agent is told to read at the moment of action is, by construction, the copy that loses.

## Message to vc-x1: duplicated cycle rules, and landing

Findings from 2026-08-12 and 2026-08-13, drafted for vc-x1's mailbox and recorded here before
delivery. Two items, sent ahead of the formal reply: the duplication compounds with every commit
either repo writes, and the landing gap is a hole this repo fell into on the 12th.

This section records a **message** rather than a commit, so it carries no as-built ladder. A
message can never be a record ([custom-family.md](../../custom-family.md#messaging)), and these
findings had no home outside a gitignored `tmp/` file. It keeps the decisions and the
measurements, and the route to them is in the session the opening commit's `ochid:` trailer
names.

### Nine steps in two files

wink's line, verbatim:

> Wink thinks the duplication of the 9 rules is guaranteeing drift in the future and we should
> contemplate eliminating the duplication

- **The overlap is nearly total.** `cycle-checklists.md` has 11 sections and almost every one
  restates a `cycle-protocol.md` section. The per-commit lists are the same nine steps in the same
  order, and `Topic bookmarks are drafts` is a section title in both files.

  | cycle-checklists.md | cycle-protocol.md |
  | --- | --- |
  | The cycle at a glance | Cycles |
  | Cycles run on a bookmark | Topic bookmarks are drafts |
  | Opening checklist | Preparation |
  | Per-commit checklist, nine steps | Per-commit flow, the same nine steps |
  | Ladder (sub-cycle) checklist | Per-Work-commit contract within a ladder |
  | Before any push | Pushing / Policy |
  | After the final push | After push or squash-push: stop and wait |
  | Close-out checklist | Close-out |

- **The reader most exposed is the one following the rules.** Hard rule 7 says read the checklist
  before acting; the checklist's own header says the protocol wins on any disagreement. So the file
  an agent is told to read at the moment of action is, by construction, the copy that loses.
- **Three instances the same day**: `custom-family.md` pointing at "step 4" after the morning's
  sync moved validation to step 5; one new rule written into both files, corrected by wink, then
  over-corrected; and a single-step cycle's chores as-built ladder and its six-item `### Ladder`
  being the same rung written twice.
- **Proposed direction**: the checklist keeps the numbered imperatives and owns them; the protocol
  drops the restatement and holds the reasoning, the recovery procedures, the close-out shapes and
  the trapezoid recipe, referring to steps by name so renumbering cannot desynchronize them.
- **The range**: the minimum is that no rule is stated twice, and wink's inclination is one file
  rather than two. We could find no written case for keeping them separate, which is what the
  message asks vc-x1 for.

### Landing, measured

Making one or more already-pushed commits permanent, with `<branch>` the bookmark that advances
and `<cycle>` the topic bookmark it advances to. Measured 2026-08-13 in a throwaway repo pair built
to that premise.

```
jj log -r '<branch>::<cycle>' -R .        # precondition; empty output means <branch> moved, stop
jj bookmark set <branch> -r <cycle> -R .  # local
jj bookmark delete <cycle> -R .           # local
jj git push -b <branch> -b <cycle> -R .   # one push, both halves
```

- **Three commands, not four.** A deletion needs no push of its own: `-b` repeats, and naming a
  locally deleted bookmark publishes its deletion. Bare `jj git push` is not a substitute, since it
  declines to publish deletions without `--deleted` or an explicit `-b`.
- **Both mutating steps are local**, so the sequence has exactly one irreversible moment.
- **Rerunning is safe, for a reason that is a trap.** A second identical run printed
  `Warning: No matching bookmarks for names: mycycle` and `Nothing changed`, and **exited 0**,
  because `-b` matches patterns rather than literal names. So a mistyped bookmark succeeds
  silently, and nothing built on this can use exit status to know the deletion happened.
- **The push's own output is the per-step report** wink wanted a command to produce: one line per
  bookmark, `move forward from ... to ...` and `delete from ...`.
- **Nothing here commits the agent repo**, which is what cost us a record on 2026-08-12. The act
  creates no work-repo commit, so nothing carried an `ochid:` and the session that decided it was
  left dangling.

### The proposal: two flags on `push`

`vc-x1 push --from <cycle> --to <branch> --delete-from` (wink, 2026-08-13), superseding a
`vc-x1 land` subcommand drafted first. The margin is too thin for a new verb: `push` already
commits both repos, advances the destination bookmark and publishes it, measured by
`vc-x1 push main --dry-run` on an empty work `@` running four of its five stages.

Three flags, one of them a rename:

- **`--to <branch>`**, the bookmark that advances, renaming `push`'s existing `[BOOKMARK]`
  positional / `--bookmark` rather than adding an argument. The positional stays as shorthand.
- **`--from <cycle>`**, the bookmark it advances to. Safety and cleanup only, never content
  selection: `bookmark-set` hardcodes `-r @-`, so what publishes is always where you stand.
  Require `<from>` to be at `@-` and refuse otherwise, and a wrong `--from` cannot publish the
  wrong thing.
- **`--delete-from`** (wink), `jj bookmark delete` being the verb a user already has, and the flag
  pairing with `--from` so the bookmark is named once. `--clean` was rejected for naming the
  working copy's state in the same breath, and `--retire` / `--retire-cycle` for inventing a
  synonym and, in the second case, hardcoding a role the other flags keep neutral.
  - Deletion stays opt-in: a default would bake our hard rule 13 into tooling documented as
    assuming nothing about a repo beyond `.jj` and `.vc-config.toml`.

Three behaviors that come with them:

- **Refuse a non-fast-forward outright**, no override flag, which also makes a swapped pair safe.
- **Derive the agent-repo commit's message from `@-`** when work `@` is empty, rather than
  demanding a title and body for a work commit that is never created.
- **Report rather than act**: the as-built backfill is due (permanence is what makes those SHAs
  stable, and the trigger has no enforcement anywhere today), and other bookmark deletions are
  pending. It must not inspect the project's records, `push` assuming nothing about a repo beyond
  `.jj` and `.vc-config.toml`.

**Nothing else changes**: the clean/dirty polymorphism already works, `commit-work` skipping when
`@` is empty and the message stage when neither repo has pending changes, so a dirty `@` needs
`--title` / `--body` and a clean one does not.

### Not building yet: an inferred `--from`

`--from` could default to the current branch, which is what it would be most of the time. It should
not, yet.

- **There is no current bookmark to infer, and it fails in both directions** (wink). At `@-` there
  may be **none**, the normal state mid-ladder where rungs are `jj new` plus `jj describe` and
  nothing is pushed; or **several**, the case below.
- **Several is guaranteed at every cycle opening rather than exotic.** The bookmark is created
  at the opening and nothing has committed on it, so it and `<branch>` sit on the same commit.
  Measured at this cycle's own opening: `docs-converge-the-agent-files-with-vc-x1` and `main` both
  on `28bd6daa`. Paired with `--delete-from`, a wrong guess deletes `main`.
- **jj declines to pick, and so should the command.** wink's shell prompt renders the set,
  `(docs-converge-the-agent-files-with-vc-x1 main+1)`, rather than naming one as current.
- So `--from` stays explicit until a written rule names what inference picks and prints what it
  inferred before acting.

### Naming

- **`land` is retired as the command's name.** It is singular in ordinary use, so a compound
  operation borrowing it promises less than it does (wink). `push-onto` was rejected too, `jj
  rebase` already using `--onto` for its destination.
- **The state sense keeps a word of its own, and the pinned text already has it**: *permanent*.
  `cycle-protocol.md` says "lands on a **permanent branch**", so "backfill once the commit is
  permanent" needs no metaphor and no glossary entry, and command and state stop borrowing from
  each other.
- The agent-files should spell the operation out rather than lean on a term: hard rule 13, the
  close-out step, and `jj.md`'s section title all use "land" as though it were defined.

### Findings carried alongside

- **Beats with no work-repo commit have no `ochid:` anchor** (wink). Landing is one; writing a
  mailbox message is worse, producing no work commit at all, and the template repo has no commits
  to archive it either. This section is that artifact, produced by hand.
- **The chores rollover trigger is undocumented.** `notes.md` gives a new file a `[1]` start and
  says nothing else. Practice across chores-01 through 06 is 552, 1264, 1088, 1342, 1178 and 1255
  lines, so the real trigger is roughly 1100 to 1300, known to us and to nobody else.
- **`prose.md#cycle-bookend-titles` is a dangling anchor in both repos.** `notes.md:190` and
  `cycle-protocol.md:196` link it, while `prose.md:234` carries the text as bold inside a paragraph
  rather than as a heading. Byte-identical on both sides, so it is the family's, and a correction
  rather than a proposal.
- **Nothing says which part of the deliberation goes where.** The pinned files send it to "chores,
  todo, and the session" without dividing them, which is how this section's first draft came out a
  transcript with headings. A line saying chores keeps decisions and measurements while the session
  keeps the route would settle it, and it is the same disease as the nine steps: content with no
  single owner.

An ordinary rebase (`jj rebase -s <root>` onto a new base, which is what we ran) moves a subtree as a unit. Internally the moved segment keeps its order, and the destination line isn't touched at all. So from the moved line's point of view, the five commits that had landed on `main` were *inserted below* the convergence opening, and everything kept its order relative to its own group. You can see it in the two listings: the five inserted commits appear in the identical order on both sides — the only thing that changed is where the one relocated commit sits relative to that block (above it in the work walk, below it in the bot journal, which never moves anything). The skew from any single rebase is always exactly that: one contiguous block displaced, all internal orders preserved.

The caveat: `jj rebase -r` (single revision) is not a pure insertion. It extracts one commit and re-parents that commit's descendants onto its *old* parent — a removal from the middle of a line. We used it for the trapezoid reshape, where it happened to preserve reading order (the close-out went from sitting above the sweep rung to being the merge above the sweep rung), but in general `-r` can change a commit's order relative to its former descendants. And jj also has explicit reordering forms (`--insert-before` / `--insert-after`) that permute on purpose — those are deliberate, not side effects.

So the practical rule for reading paired histories: after ordinary rebases, the work-vs-bot skew is always a block displacement you could visually re-align, and internal orders agree. But since `-r` and explicit reorders exist, the only assumption that's *always* safe is the one validate-desc makes — match by ochid, never by position.

The plain version: yes, a normal rebase is an insertion, and nothing above or below the inserted block gets shuffled among itself. The one exception is the single-commit form of rebase, which pulls a commit out of the middle, and that's the tool we only reach for deliberately, like the trapezoid.

##### docs: review vc-x1's agent-file set

The formal review owed since their 2026-08-08 message, plus the full reply: our answer on
whether a notes entry stays a numbered list item, becomes a heading with a real anchor, or
leaves the repo for a tracker, and a verdict on each remaining difference between the two sets.
The proposals to name have grown since the opening: the 0.24.8 validation rule, the flat
semicolon rule and its sweep (0.25.0), and the always-linked closing rung (0.25.1). The message
inviting their review of our whole set goes via `../vc-x1-messages`, absorbing the Todo entry
"Converge agent-files with vc-x1".
input.new_string:
##### docs: review vc-x1's agent-file set

**The review's result: their set is our base, and the whole diff is ours.** Every hunk across
the eight differing files was walked against their working copy (mtimes 2026-08-14, so read
rather than assumed), and each belongs to one of our three proposals: validate every commit
(0.24.8), the flat semicolon rule and its sweep (0.25.0), and the always-linked closing rung
(0.25.1). Nothing of theirs is missing from our set and nothing of theirs arrived that we have
not taken, so the verdict list is: ours to offer, three proposals. Theirs to take, none. Open,
none. `custom.md` is byte-identical, as the stub design promises.

**The notes-entry answer** (their 2026-08-12 question): an entry stays a numbered list item,
cited by its bold title with the number as a hint only, which is their own proposal and we
support it as hard rule 9's extension to the notes files. Headings would buy stable anchors at
the price of hiding the strict rank that is the list's point, and the surfaces needing real
anchors already have them, chores sections and message records both being headings. The
tracker is rejected on their own framing, independently confirmed by our messages-repo design:
issues and databases sit outside the clone, the diff, and jj history, so GitHub issues stay
held in reserve for the one job no file can do, notification.

**The mailbox swept**: their 2026-08-12 and 2026-08-08 entries handled and deleted, the file
with them. The commit-body form was adopted at 0.24.7, their two regression flags were
confirmed fixed by the 0.24.5 sync on their own measurement, and the remaining Done-whens are
answered by this cycle's records and the coming message. One operational warning is carried
forward rather than deleted with the entry: their `repos.agent` hard rename means a future
binary will refuse our `.vc-config.toml` with a fix-it message, a five-second edit at a moment
we pick.

The message inviting their review of our whole set goes via `../vc-x1-messages`, absorbing the
Todo entry "Converge agent-files with vc-x1". It delivers after landing, when its pointers have
permanent targets.

The agent-file substance all landed in 0.25.0/0.25.1, so a commit whose only content is "here is what reviewing showed" followed by a close-out that immediately moves that same text to chores is two commits' ceremony for one commit's change. Thoughts on the two options:

**Fold into the close-out as one 0.25.2 — yes.** The cycle becomes opening (0.25.2-0, already pushed) plus close-out (0.25.2). The review's findings stay exactly where they are in the block; the ladder shrinks to opening + closing, with the review recorded as a subsection of the cycle's record rather than a rung of its own — a draft-rewrite the topic-bookmark rules exist to permit. The close-out then does its normal duties (acceptance check, block moves to chores, Done entry, land) and the review text arrives in chores having been committed exactly once.

**Squash into 0.25.1 — I'd push back.** 0.25.1 is landed on `main`, belongs to a different cycle ("docs: always link the closing rung"), and has a bot twin already paired and squash-repaired once today. Folding convergence records into it means a third published-history rewrite today, a re-pairing of its bot twin, and a misfiled record — the review of vc-x1's set filed under a commit about closing rungs. The version tidiness isn't worth what it costs, and every rewrite leaves another decoder residue in the records.

That's exactly the class of repair we just spent the afternoon on, volunteered this time.

The cheap shape is **two commits**: the opening as it stands (0.25.2-0 — and it was real work: the findings section, the block, the rebase resolution all ride in it), plus one close-out at 0.25.2 carrying the review records and the close-out duties. No rewrites, no twin surgery, and the ladder reads opening + closing, which the protocol's "minimum two" explicitly blesses.

Correct — with one asymmetry to name. The work-side squash is squarely inside "topic bookmarks are drafts": pushed-to-bookmark is durable but *not published*, landing is the publication line, so reshaping the line before it lands — including collapsing a multi-step into a single-step — is exactly what the draft rules exist to permit. Nothing untoward at all; it's the same license the trapezoid reshape uses. The asymmetry: the opening's **bot twin** is not on a draft — bot `main` is linear and published — so matching it to the new single-step title is one more coordinated re-describe plus sideways push over there. Practiced today, known cost, but worth saying that the "perfectly fine" applies cleanly to the work side and by rule-4 exception to the bot side.

The sequence, stepwise with stops:

1. **Finalize the block as single-step** (working copy edits): ladder collapses to one bare-title rung, the opening/review subsections become design subsections, acceptance check runs and records its result, block moves to chores-07, Done entry written, version restamped **0.25.2**.
2. Full validation. Stop — show you the single commit's title and body.

4. Re-describe the bot twin (`ywqklntnvmoo`) to match, trailer hand-copied. Stop between each.
5. Force-push the bookmark, force-push bot `main` (each on its own go), then land — the three-command sequence — and you squash-push the tail after my hard stop.
6. Next turn: the message in `vc-x1-messages`.

Starting step 1 now.

**Why the cycle exists at all, since no `## Todo` entry moved into it.** The work is correspondence
and convergence, which no ranked entry names. Todo #4, "Sync the 20260803 agent-files baseline",
is adjacent and may be wholly overtaken by 0.24.5's sync; deciding that is this cycle's to do at
close-out rather than the opening's to assume.

**The chores file is opened at Preparation, which the protocol forbids** ("Nothing is opened in the
chores file here"). Taken as an explicit exception on wink's instruction, and recorded here per the
hard rules' preamble. The justification is that the two rules point in opposite directions for this
one beat: `custom-family.md`'s messaging rule sends a message's durable content to
`notes/chores/chores-NN.md`, while the cycle protocol reserves that file for close-out. The content
in `chores-07.md` is not this cycle's record, which stays here in `## In Progress`; it is the
record of a message, whose beat produces no commit of its own. We think that collision is a real
gap in the pinned set rather than a local awkwardness, and it goes to vc-x1 with the reply.

**Nothing retired from `## Done` at the opening sweep.** The checklist calls for one, and running
it returned nothing: all seven entries are agent-file cycles from 0.24.x, which is precisely the
nearby context a convergence cycle reads. A sweep that returns nothing is a run sweep, not a
skipped one.

**Patch scope, so 0.25.2-0** after the 2026-08-14 re-stamp (0.24.10-0 at the opening). Records,
correspondence, and at most small edits to pinned prose: work within the existing shape rather
than a reshaping of it.

and always-link cycles landed first, and the predicted conflicts (TODO.md, chores-07,

additions. The block came up to the new rules on the way: the closing rung linked with its
stub, the rung refs renumbered, and the acceptance check's stale counts refreshed. The Todo
entry "Converge agent-files with vc-x1", which main gained while this cycle was open, moved in
here, its message duty folding into the review rung.

##### docs: converge the agent-files with vc-x1 opening

`chores-07.md`: the nine-step duplication between `cycle-checklists.md` and `cycle-protocol.md`,
the undefined "land" with the sequence we actually ran, the `vc-x1 land` design, and the four
findings carried alongside. Then deliver the drafted entry to vc-x1's mailbox. The rung carries
the record because the message beat produces no commit of its own to carry it.

**The design the intent names no longer exists.** `vc-x1 land` was drafted, then superseded within
the rung by `vc-x1 push --from <cycle> --to <branch> --delete-from` (wink): `push` already commits
both repos, advances the destination and publishes it, so a new verb buys only a precondition and a
cleanup. Recording a design and discarding it inside one rung is what the rung is for.

**Four measurements replaced four assumptions**, taken in throwaway repo pairs rather than reasoned
from the docs: the sequence is three commands and not four, since `-b` repeats and a locally
deleted bookmark named in a push publishes its deletion; both mutating steps are local, so there is
one irreversible moment; a rerun warns and **exits 0**, because `-b` matches patterns, so a typo

## docs: converge the agent-files with vc-x1

- [[N]] docs: converge the agent-files with vc-x1

The 0.25.2 cycle, run single-step after its three-rung ladder collapsed: the formal review of
vc-x1's set, the answers their messages waited on, and the records that carry the convergence
proposal.

### Problem

Our pinned agent-files and vc-x1's differ, and everything that would reconcile them is owed by
us: the formal review of their set, owed since their 2026-08-08 message; two answers their
2026-08-12 message asks for; and an announcement of the rule 0.24.8 wrote into two pinned files,
which is an open proposal sitting in our diff that they have no way to see. Meanwhile the
2026-08-12 findings, the nine-step duplication and the undefined "land", exist only in a
gitignored `tmp/` file, so the repo's durable record does not hold them at all.

### Solution

The 2026-08-12 findings moved from `tmp/` into this file's message section, and the early entry
was delivered to vc-x1's template mailbox. The formal review walked every hunk of the eight-file
diff and gave each a verdict, all of it our three proposals. Their notes-entry question is
answered, the template mailbox is swept, and the review invitation goes via `../vc-x1-messages`
now that the cycle lands.

### Acceptance check

Three measures, none of which waits on vc-x1's answer:

- `diff -rq agent-data ../vc-x1/agent-data` (plus `AGENTS.md` / `custom.md`) names only files
  whose every difference this cycle's record accounts for with a verdict (ours to keep, theirs
  to take, or open with vc-x1). At the opening it was two files and three hunks, all 0.24.8's
  validation rule. After 0.25.0 and 0.25.1 the diff also carries the flat semicolon rule, its
  sweep, and the always-linked closing rung, all ours to offer.
- Nothing this cycle carries survives only in `tmp/`: every finding is in a committed file.
- The early entry sits in `../vc-x1-template/messages/vc-x1.md` (delivered at the opening), the
  full reply and review invitation are recorded via `../vc-x1-messages` per its protocol, and
  each `Done when` item of their 2026-08-12 message is either answered or named as deliberately
  not answered.

**Result: two measures pass in full, the third half-passes by construction**, 2026-08-14.
Measure 1: all eight differing files walked hunk by hunk, every difference one of the three
proposals, verdicts recorded in the review subsection below. Measure 2: the findings have lived
in this file's message section since the opening commit. Measure 3: the early entry is
delivered, while the reply's own delivery follows landing by construction, the permalink
ordering rule forbidding a pointer to an unlanded target. The abandoned 2026-08-13 close-out
draft failed this same measure outright, and the difference is that delivery is now the next
act rather than unscheduled.

### Ladder

- [[N]] docs: converge the agent-files with vc-x1

### Deliberation

**Why the cycle exists at all, since no `## Todo` entry moved into it at the opening.** The work
is correspondence and convergence, which no ranked entry named. Todo "Sync the 20260803
agent-files baseline" is adjacent and may be wholly overtaken by 0.24.5's sync; deciding that is
the convergence exchange's to do rather than this cycle's to assume. Later, `main` gained the
entry "Converge agent-files with vc-x1" while this cycle was open, and at the rebase it moved in
here.

**Collapsed to single-step at close-out** (wink): the review rung's diff was records only, the
agent-file substance having landed in 0.25.0 and 0.25.1, so the three-rung ladder became one
commit. Squashing a draft on its bookmark is what topic-bookmarks-are-drafts licenses. The
pushed opening's bot twin carried the opening title and is published, so the collapse cost one
coordinated re-describe on the bot side, accepted knowingly.

**The chores file is opened at Preparation, which the protocol forbids** ("Nothing is opened in
the chores file here"). Taken as an explicit exception on wink's instruction, and recorded per
the hard rules' preamble. The justification is that the two rules point in opposite directions
for this one beat: `custom-family.md`'s messaging rule sends a message's durable content to
`notes/chores/chores-NN.md`, while the cycle protocol reserves that file for close-out. The
message section is not this cycle's record; it is the record of a message, whose beat produces
no commit of its own. We think that collision is a real gap in the pinned set rather than a
local awkwardness, and it goes to vc-x1 with the reply.

**Nothing retired from `## Done` at the opening sweep.** Running it returned nothing: all seven
entries were agent-file cycles from 0.24.x, precisely the nearby context a convergence cycle
reads. A sweep that returns nothing is a run sweep, not a skipped one.

**Patch scope, and after two re-stamps the close-out is 0.25.2** (0.24.10-0 at the opening,
0.25.2-0 at the rebase). Records, correspondence, and at most small edits to pinned prose: work
within the existing shape rather than a reshaping of it.

**Rebased onto 0.25.1** (2026-08-14, wink's whichever-lands-second-rebases call): the semicolon
and always-link cycles landed first, and the predicted conflicts (TODO.md, chores-07,
Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock) resolved by keeping main's records and re-applying this cycle's
additions. The block came up to the new rules on the way. The same day's paired-history repairs
(two bot-side re-describes, a landing commit folded into its twin) are recorded in the review
subsection's findings and ride to vc-x1 with the message.

**The bookmark was created unpublished** (`jj bookmark set`, not `jj git push --named`), since
nothing was being pushed yet and a line nobody has approved does not need to be visible.

**Out of scope, deliberately**: folding vc-x1's answers back into our pinned copies. That waits
on their reply, so binding this cycle's close-out to it would make the close-out hostage to
another repo's session.

### The opening's record

Create the bookmark, open the block, and give the 2026-08-12 findings a durable home in the
message section above: the nine-step duplication between `cycle-checklists.md` and
`cycle-protocol.md`, the undefined "land" with the sequence we actually ran, the `vc-x1 land`
design, and the four findings carried alongside. Then deliver the drafted entry to vc-x1's
mailbox.

**The design the intent named no longer exists.** `vc-x1 land` was drafted, then superseded
within the beat by `vc-x1 push --from <cycle> --to <branch> --delete-from` (wink): `push`
already commits both repos, advances the destination and publishes it, so a new verb buys only
a precondition and a cleanup.

**Four measurements replaced four assumptions**, taken in throwaway repo pairs rather than
reasoned from the docs: the sequence is three commands and not four, since `-b` repeats and a
locally deleted bookmark named in a push publishes its deletion; both mutating steps are local,
so there is one irreversible moment; a rerun warns and **exits 0**, because `-b` matches
patterns, so a typo succeeds silently and exit status cannot be trusted; and
`vc-x1 push main --dry-run` on an empty `@` already runs four of its five stages. The first of
those corrected a recipe this beat had already written down.

**The record came out a transcript and was cut by half** (290 lines to 158) after wink called
it, which produced the beat's most general finding: nothing in the agent-files says which part
of the deliberation goes to chores, which to todo, and which to the session. They name all three
and divide none.

**Two stale bookmarks swept on the way past**, `punctuation-sweep` and `fix-calibration`, both
measured fully merged. The three that are not, one being `web-claude-tweaks` with an unlanded
commit, became the backlog's first entry rather than a claim in a record.

### The review of vc-x1's agent-file set

**The review's result: their set is our base, and the whole diff is ours.** Every hunk across
the eight differing files was walked against their working copy (mtimes 2026-08-14, so read
rather than assumed), and each belongs to one of our three proposals: validate every commit
(0.24.8), the flat semicolon rule and its sweep (0.25.0), and the always-linked closing rung
(0.25.1). Nothing of theirs is missing from our set and nothing of theirs arrived that we have
not taken, so the verdict list is: ours to offer, three proposals. Theirs to take, none. Open,
none. `custom.md` is byte-identical, as the stub design promises.

**The notes-entry answer** (their 2026-08-12 question): an entry stays a numbered list item,
cited by its bold title with the number as a hint only, which is their own proposal and we
support it as hard rule 9's extension to the notes files. Headings would buy stable anchors at
the price of hiding the strict rank that is the list's point, and the surfaces needing real
anchors already have them, chores sections and message records both being headings. The tracker
is rejected on their own framing, independently confirmed by our messages-repo design: issues
and databases sit outside the clone, the diff, and jj history, so GitHub issues stay held in
reserve for the one job no file can do, notification.

**The mailbox swept**: their 2026-08-12 and 2026-08-08 entries handled and deleted, the file
with them. The commit-body form was adopted at 0.24.7, their two regression flags were confirmed
fixed by the 0.24.5 sync on their own measurement, and the remaining Done-whens are answered by
this cycle's records and the coming message. One operational warning is carried forward rather
than deleted with the entry: their `repos.agent` hard rename means a future binary will refuse
our `.vc-config.toml` with a fix-it message, a five-second edit at a moment we pick.

**Findings from the day's own mechanics**, for the message: a work-side re-describe desyncs its
bot twin's title unless both are rewritten (measured twice, repaired twice); a `vc-x1 push` with
an empty work `@` mints a bot-only commit whose title matches no work commit, the measured
instance of the derive-from-`@-` proposal; push has no verb that publishes an amended history
without committing something, so post-surgery publishing is bare jj; and a rebase permanently
skews work-list order against the chronological bot journal, so paired-history readers must
match by ochid, never by position.

The command sequence, with expected output for each and stops between:

**1. Squash the close-out content into the opening** (work repo):
```
jj squash -R .
```
`@` has no description, so jj keeps the destination's — no editor, no prompt. ```

<approved body>

```

**3. Verify the pair-to-be**: `jj log -r ywqklntn -T description -R .claude` first, to read the bot twin's exact current trailer before overwriting (the lesson from step A this morning), then:

**4. Re-describe the bot twin** (published, so the flag is needed):
```

ochid: /pnowzztyrqks"
```
Expected: "Rebased 7 descendant commits" — everything above it in the journal rides along, change ids stable.

**5. Cross-check**: `vc-x1 validate-desc @ -n 3` in each repo — both should read `ok` with matching titles.

**6. Publish the bot repair**: `jj git push -b main -R .claude` — one "move sideways" line.

**7. Land** — and here's one economy worth your eye: I'd *skip* re-pushing the bookmark sideways first, since landing supersedes it immediately. The three-command sequence:
```
jj bookmark set main -r pnowzzty -R .
jj bookmark delete docs-converge-the-agent-files-with-vc-x1 -R .
jj git push -b main -b docs-converge-the-agent-files-with-vc-x1 -R .
```
Expected: "move forward" for `main`, "delete from" for the bookmark — the push both advances `main` and publishes the deletion, per the measured recipe.

**8. Yours, after my hard stop**: `vc-x1 squash-push -R .claude` — the session tail folds into bot `main`'s tip and pushes.
